first.rationale: Prioritize a guarded onboarding-simplification test because onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and inherited evidence indicates shortening onboarding improves completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. Verify the prior onboarding result and the pricing retention trade-off before committing; competitor pricing pressure alone does not justify a tactic with known 30-day retention harm when the objective is sustainable qualified revenue.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. It directly addresses the concurrent 4% completion decline and 6% activation decline, and the verified prior result showed completion +13%, time-to-value 2.1 days faster, and 30-day retention +3%. Do not use promotional pricing: despite acquisition and qualified-revenue lift, its verified 12% retention loss fails the sustainable-revenue objective.

final2.rationale: Maintain the onboarding-simplification experiment. The competitor's deeper cut and doubled price-related churn conversations increase urgency, but they do not establish that discounting will retain the at-risk SMB cohort. Verified pricing evidence showed a 12% 30-day retention decline and failure to survive first renewal, while verified onboarding simplification improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention. Flag the unresolved competitive-price risk rather than substituting a known unsustainable acquisition tactic.
